title: Photosynthesis
learning_goals: Describe the overall flow of photosynthesis from light capture to glucose production.
Explain how sunlight energy is converted into chemical energy (ATP and NADPH).
Identify the role of the Calvin Cycle in carbon fixation.

segments.text: Let's explore the whole photosynthesis diagram, which shows how light energy becomes sugar in a plant.
Sunlight is captured by chlorophyll pigments in the leaf.
The absorbed light drives the light‑dependent reactions.
These reactions produce the energy carriers ATP and NADPH.
ATP and NADPH are then used in the Calvin Cycle to fix carbon dioxide.
The Calvin Cycle produces glucose, the plant's stored energy.
A side product of the light‑dependent reactions is oxygen, which is released into the atmosphere.
In summary, sunlight → chlorophyll → light‑dependent reactions → ATP/NADPH → Calvin Cycle → glucose, with oxygen released along the way.
